q: What is the difference between a query builder (Kysely) and an ORM (Prisma, Drizzle)?
options: There is no difference, the words mean the same
A query builder lets you write the SQL shape in code with type checks. An ORM also has models, relations and often migrations, and writes most of the SQL for you
A query builder only works with MySQL
An ORM never produces SQL
why: Kysely's own site calls it a type-safe SQL query builder and says it is not an ORM. Under every tool here there is still SQL and a list of values.

q: You mistype a column as `total_cent`. With which tool do you find out BEFORE the program runs?
options: Raw SQL text sent with pg
Kysely or Drizzle, as a TypeScript error in the editor
None of them, every tool finds out at run time
Only Hasura
why: Raw SQL is just text until PostgreSQL runs it (`column "total_cent" does not exist`). Kysely and Drizzle know the columns, so the compiler complains first.

q: Why do values go in `$1` and not into the SQL text?
options: It makes the query run faster in every case
A value pasted into the text can become SQL (injection). A parameter is sent apart and is always treated as a value
Because SQL cannot contain numbers
Because `$1` encrypts the value
why: Text like `paid'; DROP TABLE orders; --` is harmless as a parameter. Pasted into the text it becomes a command.

q: A user may pick the sort column of a list. Can you bind it as `ORDER BY $1`? What do you do?
options: Yes, `$1` works for column names
No, `$1` binds values only. Check the name against an allow list, then put it in the text
Yes, but only for `asc` and `desc`
Never allow sorting
why: Names (tables, columns, asc and desc) cannot be parameters. A builder checks them against the schema. Without one, you must keep an allow list yourself.

q: A page runs 101 queries for 100 stores. The ORM code type-checks fine. Why does nothing warn you, and what do you do?
options: Types do not see query counts. Read the query log, and load the relation in one call (for example `include`, or a JOIN)
The type checker is broken, so reinstall it
ORMs never cause N+1
Switch to a different ORM and the problem goes away
why: An ORM hides the SQL, including how many queries it sends. Lesson 12 has the fixes. Every tool here can have an N+1 if you loop and query.

q: You find a two-year-old tutorial for a Prisma setup. What do you check before you copy it?
options: Nothing, setup never changes
The version in the tutorial, and the tool's current release status and docs
Only the author's name
Only the number of likes
why: Prisma 7 changed how the client is built and made driver adapters required, and Prisma 8 is a release candidate with a new API. Check the version and the current docs.
